question: In its communication COM(2025) 805 final of 23 December 20251, the Commission shared concerns voiced by European recyclers about virgin plastics being sold as recycled. It outlined new measures, including separate customs codes, audits and support for laboratories in order to determine whether imports being declared as recycled PET are indeed recycled.

In its answer2 to question E-000567/20263 on 24 April 2026, the Commission referred to these measures, but did not include any figures on the number of inspections carried out. If we want to protect our recycling companies and the jobs they provide, these statements need to be translated into concrete action. In light of the above: 1.
How much progress has the Commission made on the separate customs codes planned for the second quarter of 2026, which products will they apply to and how soon will they be available?

What data has it collected since January 2026 on the number of lots inspected and analysed, the number of false declarations identified and the follow-up action taken, listed by Member State of inspection and by country of origin?
What audits and analytical methods has it used, and how will it ensure that equivalent fraud detection capabilities are put in place at entry points across the Union?
